exposure: Prenatal and early-life fecal microbiome composition
cohort: 657 mother-child pairs from the Vitamin D Antenatal Asthma Reduction Trial
finding: Specific maternal and infant fecal microbial taxa were associated with different childhood asthma phenotypes, and a longitudinal gut microbiome profile was linked to early asthma development, highlighting the role of the early-life fecal microbiome in asthma risk.
mod_finding: While not directly associated with asthma, cesarean section was found to reduce fecal Bacteroides and microbial sphingolipids, potentially increasing susceptibility to early asthma.
